conviction_note: The FY26 numbers are already out (pre-close 16 Sep: headline PBT c.GBP75m, net debt c.GBP325m), so the move depends on the first FY27 guide and on Executive Chair Leo Quinn's first set of priorities. No FY27 consensus could be sourced, so the bar is unknown. I sized the move at 8% because this is a guidance event, the short is crowded at 11.5% and the guidance-line reactions over the past year ran 7-16%. p_up is 47, not 50: the name sold all three guidance events in the past year, the stock is up 10.6% over 20 days and a new chair has a reason to guide low. That puts the scaled number at -0.48 against a findings sum of +1.0. The findings are small proxy positives (peer current trading, documented self-help, a crowded short) and none of them can fix the sign against an unsourced bar.

FY27 net debt and free-cash-flow targets, and the working-capital unwind. Unknown.

The impairment of up to GBP150m, already flagged, and any update on the FCA investigation. Expected inside the flagged range.
Possible portfolio decisions (strategic options for Welcome to Las Vegas, the InMotion review, ROW exits). Unknown.

findings.finding: Direct peers that reported after WHS's pre-close show travel-retail trading firming into WHS's FY27 Q1: SSP's Jul-Sep Q4 had UK&I LFL +9% and North America +2% ('outperforming the market'), and Avolta reported October organic growth of about +4% with all regions contributing. That points to current trading in the prelims being better than WHS's own Q4 (UK +4%, NA -3%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Current-trading and guidance statements moved SMWH -9.15% (interims, 2026-04-23), -16.17% (June trading update) and +0.44% (Sept pre-close, in line) over the past year.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: both peer releases are public, and SMWH rose from 373p to 426p over Oct 14-20. But it has given back 6.8% in the last 5 sessions, and the transmission is a hypothesis: SSP is food and beverage, and WHS's weak spot is discretionary InMotion and Las Vegas Resorts, which no peer reports. A fully priced read would not have left the stock 7% off its November high.

findings.finding: Disclosed net short of 11.48%, flat on the week, held mostly by quant and multi-strategy funds, going into a release whose FY26 profit, net debt, impairment and dividend are already disclosed. The only large unknown left is the FY27 guide, so anything short of a cut gives a squeeze fuel that a cut does not.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 16 Sep pre-close (bottom of range, no cut) moved +0.44% with the short in place, so no squeeze on an in-line statement.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: this is the baseline's own short_squeeze lean component (+3.0). Filed small only for the asymmetry that the pre-release has removed the FY26 downside lines. If the market had priced a squeeze, the stock would not sit 7% below its 4 Nov close of 447p.

findings.finding: Company documents list FY27 profit mechanics that need no market recovery: central cost reductions and lower interest costs (pre-close), exits of loss-making stores (H1 ROW trading profit was -GBP4m pre-IFRS16; Norway gone; Denmark, Sweden and the Netherlands exiting in 2027; Resorts fashion stores closed), the Cult Pens sale, and net debt cut from GBP496m (Feb) to c.GBP325m. Together they support a first FY27 guide above FY26's c.GBP75m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The first FY26 guide at the Dec 2025 prelims ('flat profit') moved -7.01%. Every guidance event since moved -9% to -16%, apart from the in-line pre-close at +0.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: The mechanics are public and sell-side FY27 numbers probably include them. No FY27 consensus could be sourced, so whether a guide built on them beats the bar is unknown. Capped small because the bar is unsourced. A new executive chair focused on 'restoring confidence' can also rebase low, which argues against this finding and is why it is not larger.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The small proxy positives agree with the +2.6 priced lean (mostly the short-squeeze term). The +10.6% 20-day run-up and a year of guidance events being sold cut against them, which is why the scaled number is slightly negative while the findings sum is positive.
language_note: Investegate (domestic RNS mirror) carried the primary texts the English wire summaries compress: the exact Q4 divisional LFL table, the 'up to GBP150m' impairment wording, and the 12 November date with 'update on key priorities for the year ahead'. Wire copy and ii/AJ Bell carried the RBC GBP78m consensus, which the RNS does not.
The FCA per-holder file showed who is short (mostly quant and multi-strategy, built after the June raise), which no English article carried.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide / a first guide for a new fiscal year is a guidance event': abs_move_pct raised from 7.0 to 8.0
'Positioning is the thing to beat, not the thing to agree with': the crowded-short finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3, because it restates the baseline's short_squeeze component
'A narrow proxy loses / macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis': the peer current-trading finding cut from +0.6 to +0.5
'Verified fact is not a predicted reaction' plus a reaction history of guidance events sold: p_up moved from 48 to 47
'A finding about a number already told is worth 0': confirmed the FY26 PBT finding at 0.0 (unchanged)
